data.name: Hero.Copy
data.value: Persistent Knox County worlds on dedicated allocation. Workshop collections resolved for you, provisioning handled by software, and a control panel that treats your server like the running system it is.

data.name: World.Body1
data.value: A Project Zomboid world is a long-lived simulation, not a match. Map state, safehouses, vehicles and loot are written to storage that outlives restarts, build changes and rebuilds of the instance underneath it.

data.name: World.Body2
data.value: When you roll a mod back, your community does not roll back with it. Restore points are taken on a schedule, and the world you return to is the world you left.

data.name: Workshop.Body
data.value: Adding a mod to a Project Zomboid server normally means finding it on the Workshop, copying two different identifiers out of the page, pasting them into two different config lines and getting the order right. Our panel does that part. You search, you press install, and the server is configured on its next restart.

data.value: Talk to the people building it

data.name: Closing.ContactCopy
data.value: Describe your community - how many players, how heavily you mod, how you like to play - and we will match it to the right plan, or price a build that is not on the list.

data.name: Stage01.Detail
data.value: Your configuration is captured the moment you confirm it - region, slot count, sandbox rules and mod list all travel together as one order.

data.name: Stage02.Detail
data.value: The order is released to the provisioner as soon as billing clears. Nothing waits in a queue for a human to approve it.

data.name: Stage03.Detail
data.value: The platform picks a healthy node with enough headroom for your allocation and reserves your CPU, memory and storage before anything is installed.

data.name: Stage04.Detail
data.value: The game panel builds the instance: runtime, game files, your Workshop collection and your server configuration, applied in one pass.

data.name: Stage05.Detail
data.value: Health checks pass, the world generates, and the connection details come straight back to you. No ticket, no hand-off.

data.name: Cap01.Body
data.value: A large Workshop collection should not turn server setup into a second job. Paste a collection, and the platform resolves the item list, writes the mod and Workshop identifiers in the right order, and keeps them in step every time you change something.

data.name: Cap02.Body
data.value: Map state, safehouses and loot live on storage that survives restarts, version changes and rebuilds of the instance underneath it. Rolling a mod back does not mean rolling your community back.

data.name: Cap03.Headline
data.value: Every knob, none of the FTP

data.name: Cap03.Body
data.value: Sandbox rules, INI configuration, player permissions and the live console all sit in one panel. The things you would normally email support about are buttons instead.

data.name: Cap04.Body
data.value: Server builds are handled as configurable environments rather than one fixed version, so an instance can follow the build your community actually plays. We will publish exactly which builds are selectable at launch.

data.name: Faq.Mods.Question
data.value: Can I install Project Zomboid mods?

data.name: Faq.Mods.Answer
data.value: Yes. Steam Workshop items and standalone mods can be added from the control panel, which keeps the Workshop and mod identifier lists in sync for you. Load order stays editable, so you can reorder or disable an item without rewriting server configuration by hand.

data.name: Faq.Build42.Answer
data.value: Server builds are handled as configurable environments rather than one fixed version, so an instance can be pointed at the build your community plays. As Build 42 stabilises we will publish exactly which builds are selectable at launch.

data.name: Faq.Panel.Question
data.value: Can I manage my server through a control panel?

data.name: Faq.Panel.Answer
data.value: That is the core of the product. Power actions, resource usage, live console output, configuration and file access are all designed to live in a single web panel that works on desktop and on mobile.

data.name: Faq.Restart.Question
data.value: Can the server be restarted remotely?

data.name: Faq.Restart.Answer
data.value: Yes. Start, restart and stop actions are available from the panel at any time, and scheduled restarts can be configured so your world resets on a rhythm that suits your community.

data.name: Faq.Automatic.Answer
data.value: Deployment is an automated pipeline. Once a server is created the platform reserves capacity, installs the game files, applies your configuration and reports back when health checks pass, without manual intervention.

data.name: Faq.Pricing.Question
data.value: Are the plans and prices on this page final?

data.name: Faq.Pricing.Answer
data.value: Eight tiers, 4 GB to 16 GB of memory. Storage is 25 GB up to the 6 GB tier and 40 GB from 8 GB up. The prices are not eight separate decisions: each one is a published rate card - CPU, memory and NVMe - applied to what that tier actually ships, so a plan cannot be repriced without repricing what it is made of.

data.name: Faq.Migrate.Question
data.value: Can I migrate an existing server?

data.name: Faq.Migrate.Answer
data.value: Bringing an existing world across is a supported goal for launch. The intended flow is to upload your current save and configuration, then validate the world on the new instance before you point players at it. Talk to us about your setup and we will confirm the details.

data.name: Bot.Lede
data.value: Servers configured with more than 5 GB of memory can run our own server-side management bot, built here rather than bought in. It sits alongside the world and exists to help hold performance steady as players, mods and saved state accumulate.

data.name: Bot.Caveat
data.value: What it does not do is promise a number. There is no optimisation percentage, no uptime figure and no claim that a world cannot slow down - only software whose job is to watch for it and help you act.
